$comment: D-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-MULTI-ARTIFACT (c171): the FIRST multi-artifact corpus example, across FOUR targets. Each target's `dependsOn` builds `dsslib.c` (exporting dss_lib_answer) into a STATIC LIBRARY via the c171-D `-staticlib` format (a `.lib` on pe64 / a `.a` on elf64 x86_64 + aarch64 and on macho64 arm64), then builds `main.c` (extern dss_lib_answer) RESOLVING against it via --resolve-library -> the c169/c170 COFF / c165 ELF static-link pulls the member into a SELF-CONTAINED exec -> exit 42. Witnesses, at the corpus tier + end-to-end: the c171 dependsOn runner capability, the c171-D staticlib driver surface, and the static-link pull/merge. RUNTIME per leg: PE runs natively on the Windows gate; ELF x86_64 runs natively under WSL / on the ubuntu leg; ELF aarch64 runs under qemu-aarch64 (the emulator) / on the ubuntu-24.04-arm leg -- the arm64 arm is the runnable witness that CLOSES D-LK-STATIC-LINK-AARCH64-RUNTIME (arm64 static-link had been build-only); MACH-O arm64 runs NATIVELY on the darwin leg. SkippedCrossHost where a leg cannot run, with the BUILD still giving structural coverage. D-TEST-EXAMPLES-DEPENDSON-UNCOVERED-ON-DARWIN: the macho64 arm is the entry that makes the `dependsOn` path RUN on darwin at all. Before it, NEITHER dependsOn manifest carried a `darwin` runOn, so integrated_tests' `buildDependsOnArtifactCli` -- which SKIPS an example outright when no target's runOn matches the host -- was reached by ZERO checks on the leg this project gates on every cycle: a whole build path free to rot while the suite reported green. MEASURED on darwin arm64: dsslib.a (422 B) built, main linked resolving it, spawned -> exit 42. RED-ON-DISABLE (MEASURED, same host): drop the `--resolve-library` (i.e. lose the dependsOn thread) and main STILL links -- DSS does not yet fail loud on an undefined exec symbol (the open D-LINK-EXEC-UNDEFINED-SYMBOL-FAIL-LOUD gap) -- but dyld aborts at RUNTIME with `Symbol not found: _dss_lib_answer` -> exit 134 != 42 -> the exit-code assert fires -> red. So 42 here is a real function of the archive pull, not a constant. D-EXAMPLES-DEPENDSON-NO-RELEASE-OPTIMIZER-ARM (the `release` arm below): this manifest and fat_archive_merge's are the corpus's ONLY two that use the runner's per-target `dependsOn` key, and until now NEITHER declared an `optimizedPipelines` arm -- so the whole `dependsOn` / `-staticlib` / `--resolve-library` static-link path had only ever been compiled through the baseline pipeline, which is a bare `Identity`, i.e. a no-op. WHAT THE ARM IS FOR: with the runner building each prerequisite library under the arm's OWN configuration, the `release` arm compiles `dsslib.c` through the shipped release pipeline as well as `main.c`, so the archive member the static link pulls into the exec is release-pipeline output instead of baseline output -- the first time the shipped optimizer reaches the staticlib MIR shapes on any leg, which is what lets a future optimizer regression over them RED here instead of passing green. WHY THE ARM CAN ATTRIBUTE ITS DIFFERENCE TO THE LIBRARY: `main.c` is deliberately thin -- one extern declaration and one call, no locals, no arithmetic, no inlinable callee -- so it offers the pipeline nothing of its own, while `dss_lib_answer` in dsslib.c carries an inlinable helper, a loop-invariant addend and locals for Mem2Reg to promote, and still returns exactly 42. `mustDifferFromBaseline: true` is therefore aimed AT THE PREREQUISITE BUILD: if the runner stops threading the arm's configuration into it, or if someone simplifies `dss_lib_answer` back to `return 42;`, the expectation is that the optimized exec has nothing left to differ by and the arm REDS instead of quietly asserting x == x. That expectation is INFERRED, not measured here -- but it rests on a DSS measurement of exactly this shape, recorded under D-TEST-CORPUS-77-OPTIMIZED-ARMS-WITNESS-NOTHING: a consumer whose only call was external produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL pe64 image under `debug` and `release`, and only giving the consumer an inlinable helper, an accumulator and a loop made the two configs diverge. WHAT THE PER-DEPENDENCY OPT-IN ADDS OVER THE ARM-LEVEL ONE, now that every `dependsOn` entry above also carries `mustDifferFromBaseline: true`: the ARM-LEVEL key compares the EXECUTABLE's bytes, and an exec can differ between the two configs for reasons entirely its own -- main.c's translation unit, image layout, anything the pipeline touches on the consumer side -- so a green arm-level assertion is still consistent with `dsslib.c` having been built at BASELINE the whole time. Only the PER-DEPENDENCY key compares THE PREREQUISITE'S OWN IMAGE, arm vs baseline, so it is the only form here that actually asserts the ARCHIVE was compiled through the arm's pipeline; the arm-level key cannot tell that case apart from a consumer-only difference. The key is opt-in (absent means report-only) and is honoured at every nesting depth. NO corpus dependency declared it before this manifest and fat_archive_merge's, so it shipped exercised only by the two runners' planted fixtures -- these are the first corpus dependencies to arm it. SAFE TO ARM, MEASURED (shipped CLI, Windows host, cross-compiling `dsslib.c` to each `-staticlib` and comparing debug vs release BYTE-wise, not by size): pe64-x86_64 866 -> 664, elf64-x86_64 1672 -> 1464, elf64-aarch64 1512 -> 1376, macho64-arm64 770 -> 650 -- all four DIFFER, so no armed entry is a guaranteed red. That is an image measurement, NOT a leg result. Do not re-quote those byte counts as a pin: a COFF archive embeds the source stem, so the pe64 figure moves if the file is renamed; what is asserted is the DIFFERENCE, never the size. D-LINK-NONEXTERNAL-DEFINED-SYMBOL-READ-AS-BLOCK-LABEL-NOT-ATOM -- WHY `dss_lib_step` IS `static`, RESTORED 2026-08-20 (cycle P22) IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE READER FIX IT WITNESSES. The keyword IS the test. A file-local function CALLED from an exported one, inside an ARCHIVE MEMBER, is the shape the COFF and Mach-O archive-member readers used to demote to a bodyless interior block label, so its bytes never entered the image and the exec link red with `error[K_SymbolUndefined] ... relocation in CU #N targets symbol #M which is not defined or imported in that CompilationUnit` on pe64-x86_64 and macho64-arm64, while both elf64 legs linked fine because `elf::readRelocatableObject` builds an AssembledFunction from any STT_FUNC with non-zero size regardless of binding. Without the keyword the helper is an ordinary external, which every reader has always promoted to an atom, so this example would build, link and exit 42 while asserting NOTHING about the readers -- and a `static` helper in an archived TU is the ubiquitous shape, what any C author writes. MEASURED 2026-08-20 WITH THE KEYWORD (shipped CLI, this host, baseline config): the `-staticlib` build and the `--resolve-library` exec link both return rc=0 on pe64-x86_64, elf64-x86_64, elf64-aarch64, macho64-arm64 AND macho64-x86_64, and the pe64 executable runs exit 42 at both configurations. ⚠⚠ THE WITNESS IS THE BASELINE ARM AND THE `release` ARM CANNOT REACH THIS DEFECT. MEASURED with `nm` over the two archives this manifest builds: at baseline the member carries `dss_lib_answer` plus the file-local helper as a LOCAL `sym_<id>` -- DSS renames internal-linkage functions, so that is the only spelling a symbol dump will show -- and the intra-member relocation against it is exactly what the reader must resolve; at `--config=release` that local symbol is ABSENT FROM THE ARCHIVE ENTIRELY, because Inlining removes the call and DCE removes the function, so no file-local relocation survives and the arm would link green against a reader that still had the bug. The `release` arm above is still doing its own job -- the optimizer witness described earlier in this comment -- but it is not this one. `examples/c/staticlib_file_local_atoms` is the example built to hold at BOTH configurations, and it is where the silent arm, the file-local DATA half and the interior-label boundary are covered. Leg-by-leg results are NOT recorded here -- whoever runs the legs writes them.
